title: Telemetry-driven runtime gating for mixed-precision attention kernels
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: reduce end-to-end token latency and dequant overhead by dynamically selecting the optimal attention kernel (INT8 fast path vs FP8/FP16 fallback) per-request and per-segment using short-window telemetry signals. The feature should avoid unnecessary dequantization passes, minimize oscillation between kernels, and provide clear observability for rollouts.
motivation_and_background: We observe that a sizeable fraction of streaming decode requests pay repeated costs for dequant<->fp32 conversions when kernels are switched globally or when microbatches mix precision needs. Prior attempts at static selection improved average cost but caused tail latency regressions for spikes and heterogeneous workloads. A telemetry-driven gate can make selection local and adaptive while leveraging cached quantized accumulators to avoid repeated dequantization.
design_notes:
- Collect a short-window (100ms-1s) telemetry view per route: median token decode latency, per-token variance, and kv-cache hit ratio.
- Maintain a small runtime decision state: last_chosen_kernel, warmup_counter, and a decay-weighted latency estimate.
- Gate rules: prefer INT8 kernel if weighted latency benefit > threshold and warmup_counter >= min_warmup. Fall back to FP8 when error rate or variance exceeds tolerance.
- Kernel-level optimization: keep per-stream quantized accumulators (int8/uint8) and scale metadata so decode can bypass dequant when staying on quantized path. Only materialize fp32 when switching or when requested by model config.
- Hysteresis: implement minimum hold time and exponential backoff after a kernel flip to prevent thrash.
- Telemetry tagging: annotate traces with chosen_kernel, reason (latency/quality/kv), and scoring values for offline analysis.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Complexity: adds runtime state and gating logic that could increase code paths and surface bugs.
- Memory: maintaining quantized accumulators per-stream increases memory footprint; must bound by LRU or per-route caps.
- Accuracy risk: some models show minor token-level score differences on INT8; we must tie gating to quality checks for sensitive customers.
- Observability burden: requires new dashboards and alerts to detect oscillation or regressions.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end median decode latency reduced by >=10% on mixed-precision workloads in perf cluster compared to baseline without gating
95th-percentile latency not regressing by more than 5% under synthetic traffic spikes
No increased token-level hallucination rate beyond threshold on internal evals for gated routes (quality regressions < 0.5% on benchmark prompts)
Telemetry tags emitted for >99% of gated requests and visible in runtime traces
Feature can be toggled per-route via runtime config and rolled back within 5 minutes
tasks: Spec telemetry schema and sampling frequency
Implement runtime gating state machine and policy APIs
Modify attention kernels to optionally bypass dequant using cached quantized accumulators
Add LRU-bound cache for per-stream quant accumulators and eviction metrics
Add holdup/hysteresis timers and backoff logic
Build unit + integration tests with synthetic mixed-precision traces
Run perf/job in perf cluster and collect baseline vs gated comparison
Create Console dashboards: per-route gate ratio, kernel selection distribution, latency delta, and oscillation alerts
Create rollout playbook and canary config
testing_plan:
- Unit tests: state transitions, hysteresis, scale metadata correctness.
- Integration: end-to-end on small perf cluster with mixture of INT8-friendly and INT8-hostile workloads.
- A/B rollout: 10% of traffic for two weeks, measure latency & quality metrics.
- Fault injection: simulate telemetry loss and forced kernel flips to validate safe defaults.
- Regression: run existing quantization regression suite and language-model eval sets.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated behind per-route flag; 2) Canary (10%) on non-critical routes; 3) Gradual ramp with automated guardrails; 4) Full enable for routes that pass acceptance. Emergency rollback via console toggle.
monitoring_and_alerting:
- Dashboards: 'telemetry-gate/route/*' showing chosen_kernel ratio, median/95 latency, flip-rate per minute.
- Alerts: flip-rate > 0.5/min for 5m, median latency regression > 10% for 3m, quality eval failure above threshold.
- Logs: decision_reason and scoring_values emitted as structured logs for offline auditing.
